articles.title: The Bellwood Chapel Announces New Hours for Winter
articles.deck: Residents of Hickory Ridge filled the hall on Sunday to ask questions about the plan.
body: The plan calls for street tree planting along Quincy Avenue, with work expected to start in June.
Public works estimates the work will take about 27 weeks once it begins. Organizers say the project is on schedule and that volunteers are still needed on Sunday mornings.
The Hickory Ridge Improvement Group will post updates on its bulletin board outside the library. The group has raised $48,000 so far and is asking for help with supplies and food.

articles.title: Then & Now: Millrace Green, 1985 and 2011
articles.deck: A photo from the Millrace County Historical Society shows the same corner as it looked decades ago.
body: Most of the houses are still standing, though the porches and the trees have changed a good deal. A 1985 photograph from the Millrace County Historical Society shows Crane Terrace from the corner of Tillman Avenue.
Someone took the same picture from the same spot this month, holding the camera at about the same height.
Most of the houses are still standing, though the porches and the trees have changed a good deal.

articles.title: Letter: The Stormwater Drain Repair on Eaton Court Needs Attention
body: To the editor: I have lived on Eaton Court for 40 years, and I want to say what a difference the Stonebridge Trail Crew has made.
I hope the council will listen to the people who turned out at the August meeting. Thank you for printing this letter, and for all the work the paper does to keep us informed.
Marcus Jurgens, Canal Park

articles.title: Hickory Ridge Asks Council for Speed Limit Change
articles.deck: The vote came after 9 residents spoke at Sunday’s session.
body: Residents of Hickory Ridge said they had been asking for action for years, and several brought photographs of the street. Public works estimates the work will take about 9 weeks once it starts in November.

Councilmember Sadie Eckhart asked for more time to review the proposal, which would cost about $850. The ordinance will return to the agenda at the next regular session, unless the chair calls a special meeting first.
Staff recommended approval with two conditions: a traffic study and a public notice period of 30 days.
